summary:
plan.md is written; I didn't build or render it. Rotunda: an open ring of 8 arches (12 wide, 25 high), 16 giant granite-shafted columns, a relief attic and a ribbed terracotta dome 47 across (peak y 68) with a coffered underside lit by glowstone.
Colonnade: buff paired columns (16 wide bays that repeat end to end) under an entablature, an open planter box with vines and four weeping figures; a closing pier with niches ends it, and the hall bay is a blind-arched wall with a parapet and a hand-built lean-to roof.
It reads as the Palace of Fine Arts because of the salmon dome above the ring of arches, the red column shafts against warm sandstone, and the colonnade with its planter boxes. Kit of four modules: octagonal rotunda (ring, 16 granite giant columns, attic, ribbed terracotta dome, coffers), tiling peristyle bay, peristyle end with niche pier, tiling exhibition hall bay. Sandstone body, granite shafts, terracotta dome.

Rotunda ring and ground: parts/ring.mjs builds the rotunda's octagonal ring (y1..33) with a sandstone plinth, upright stair moulding and the 8 round arches carved by not placing. It also lays the floor medallion over the paving. make.sh gives 17576 placed, no refusals, no off-palette blocks. The render reads as an arched octagon.
polish: Ring top y30..33 is a flat band (cut_sandstone y30, smooth_sandstone y31..33); the columns part must add the cornice stairs, tablets and break-outs outside it.
Column base cells (4x4, y1..2) are left clear for the columns part.
Archivolts, inner pilasters and the lanterns on the pier faces are not built (ornament part).

waste.what: Wrote my own face-selection (which of the 8 faces a ring cell belongs to) and the stair-moulding outer-edge detection; also had to import B from the build library because vocab.mjs does not export it.
waste.cost: about 40 lines and 1 failed make run
waste.tool: A vocab helper such as octFaceOf(dx, dz) -> {face, t, n}, plus octRing taking an arch spec and a plinth-stairs option, with B re-exported from vocab.mjs.

companions.task: Plinth stair moulding at the corners of the diagonal faces, where the stairs only approximate the diagonal edge.

summary:
Rotunda columns and entablature: Rotunda columns and entablature (parts/columns.mjs) is built: 16 granite giant columns with bases, chiseled capitals and abacus; 8 outer and 8 inner archivolts with keystones, jambs and inner pilasters.</summary>
<parameter name="summary">Rotunda columns and entablature (parts/columns.mjs) is built: 16 granite giant columns (bases, chiseled capitals, abacus), 8 outer archivolts with keystones and jambs, and 8 inner archivolts with pilasters.
Entablature break-outs over each column (architrave y30, frieze y31..33) and the cornice at y33 with ledge slabs at y34 are in place.
make.sh saves a whole build.nbt; my part reports 5768 placed, 0 refused on its own writes, 0 off-palette; `mcd fit` is OK.
polish: Spandrel roundels (chiseled 2x2 at |t|=9.5, y25..26) are not built: they would replace smooth_sandstone that the ring part has locked.
The inner entablature band's chiseled tablet at y33 is not built, for the same reason: the ring part's y31..33 is smooth_sandstone.
Frieze tablets (chiseled over each column break-out, y31..32) are not built; the break-outs are plain smooth_sandstone.

Column capitals lose their outer row at z=5 (or the matching face row): that cell is ring-locked, so the writes are refused (about 8 refused per N/S column). Archivolt writes also refused 416 cells, from overlaps with the shafts and the ring (counted, not fixed).
plan.md inconsistency: shafts at z 3..4 touch the ring's outer face at z 5, but the plan says '1-cell clear'. I kept the listed numbers and noted it in plan.md's Notes.
Lanterns under the arch crowns (y24) are left to the lamp parts: nothing above them except the locked keystone, so they would hang in air.

waste.what: Break-out blocks over each column (4x4 at y30..33, outside the octagon) were written cell by cell with g.set loops, with an air check per cell.
waste.cost: about 200 cells in 16 loops, plus a footprint test I worked out by hand
waste.tool: A vocab helper such as entablatureBreakout(g, shaftMin, {y0, y1, layers}) that returns the cells outside a given footprint, so a part does not need its own writer.

waste.what: Helper return shapes are inconsistent: corinthianCol and cornice return a bare count, archivolt returns {placed, refused}, and I had to handle both in the loop.
waste.cost: two retries of the summary line; no blocks lost
waste.tool: Give every vocab helper the same return shape { placed, refused } (as archivolt and peristyleCol already do).

waste.what: Working out which cells were locked by the ring and which were free (capital rows at z=5, archivolt overlaps with shafts) took a render plus reading the refusal counts, rather than a report by cell.
waste.cost: one render and about 3 minutes
waste.tool: A pre-check, such as `mcd plan`-style, that lists for a part's helpers which target cells an earlier part already fills, before anything is written.

waste.what: Checking the plan's column geometry against the ring by hand (shaft at z 3..4 against ring starting at z 5, while the plan says 1-cell clear) cost a reread of plan.md.
waste.cost: one reread of the plan
waste.tool: A plan lint that compares each listed coordinate range with the earlier parts' footprints and flags touching or overlapping masses.

companions.task: Carve the spandrel roundels (chiseled 2x2 at |t|=9.5, y25..26) and the frieze tablets over each column break-out, which need the ring's smooth_sandstone opened up or a pre-cut slot in the ring part.
Make the diagonal-face cornice stairs turn correctly at the octagon's corners, where the cornice helper picks only one of the four neighbour directions.
Light the rotunda arches: lanterns on the arch-crown faces and on the pier faces at y 8, once the ring and column parts are merged and the crown can carry a hanging lantern.

summary:
Attic and dome: Attic and dome (parts/dome.mjs) built: coffers, drum y34..45 with 8 relief panels and figures, 8 corner statue piers, the y44/45 cornice, and the salmon dome shell with step rings, ribs and crown.
make.sh ran clean: the dome part placed 15,327 blocks with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines. Tiles read as the drum on its arches and the ribbed dome; the north panel zoom shows a recessed frame with three figures.
plan.md part 3 ticked, elements 6, 7 and 8 marked done, and a Notes line added.
polish: Dome-tread lanterns at y50, 56 and 62 (beside each rib) are not placed: a standing lantern needs a block under it, which the sloped shell does not give. Light inside comes from the coffer glowstone.
The plan's separate attic top deck at y46 is not built as its own row: the Pantheon step rings (y46 cut_sandstone, y47 smooth_sandstone) cover r > 23.5, and the dome base covers the rest.

$MCD check reports 59 orphans: the coffer inner-layer smooth_sandstone ribs, which touch only the brown middle band. That is the design, not a fault, but a reviewer may want the ribs tied to the shell.

waste.what: Re-derived the octagon membership test, the face normal and tangent tables, and the 'air-only' writer for my own cornice and stair loops, because vocab does not export them (inOct, faceVecs, planeOf and writer are private in h1/h2).
waste.cost: About 40 lines of duplicated geometry in dome.mjs, and one reread of h1/h2 source to get the face and tangent conventions right.
waste.tool: Export inOct, faceVecs/planeOf, and the writer from vocab/h1.mjs (or a drumRing(g, {s0, s1, y0, y1, block, skip}) helper), so the attic cornice and stair ring needs no local octagon code.

waste.what: Had to work out by hand that reliefPanel can only replace my drum cells through its over list, and that the recess layer must be skipped in the drum's octRing, so the relief reads recessed without a carve pass.
waste.cost: One design pass and one render check of the zoomed panel; no retries after that.
waste.tool: A reliefPanel option that carves its own outer recess (clear-then-fill) or an octRing skip helper keyed to a panel, so the drum and the relief don't need to agree by hand.

waste.what: Checked the stair facing for the cornice ring by hand: inward on the dominant axis, with the diagonal cells approximated.
waste.cost: About 6 lines of logic.
waste.tool: A cornice helper that takes a ring (rIn, rOut) and an inward-facing rule, as in vocab h2 cornice but for octagonal rings.

companions.task: Place the dome-tread lanterns at y50/56/62 beside each rib (no block under them on the sloped shell, so they need a support or a bracket chosen per tread) and check the drum's outside light, which the coffer glowstone does not cover.
Carve the relief panel recess and figure detail (frame depth, column backs, the statue-pier heads) once the shape is settled, since the panel reads as recessed but is still plain at close range.

summary:
Peristyle bay and end columns: Peristyle bay (plot 1) and end (plot 2) built in parts/peristyle.mjs: four peristyleCol pairs per plot, architrave, frieze with chiseled tablets, walkway soffit with cross-beams, cornice with return, deck slabs, and the closing pier body with plinth and NE/SE quoins.
Niches are carved as air for P5. make.sh saves a whole build.nbt; this part placed 4398 blocks with 0 refused and 0 off-palette; check shows no floating or unsupported blocks and fit is OK.
Plan.md and elements.md ticked for elements 11 and 12, with a Notes line. Renders read as a colonnade with a cornice and a pier with carved niches.
polish: Walkway and bay-seam lanterns (soffit lanterns at y20: x71..72 z8, x64 z9, plot 2 x80) are not placed; plan's peristyle lighting, to the lighting pass (P6/P3) or the planters part.
Niche fit-out is left to P5: chiseled sills at y3 and lanterns on the sills inside the carved north (x91..93 z2..3) and east (x93..94 z7..9) niches, which I left as air.
Pier parapet x91..94 z3..14 y25..26 and the planter boxes and weeping figures are not built here; their deck cells (box x67..76 and 80..89 at z4..13, figure cells, parapet) were left bare of slabs.

Plan rhythm note: plot 2 pairs (shafts 82/86) do not continue plot 1's pair rhythm (69/73 within a 16-wide bay), so the bay seam at x79/80 has a wider gap than inside a bay. Built as plan.md states; the planner should confirm.
Quoins at the closing pier are approximate: alternating long and short courses on the x94 column only, not true two-face rustication.

waste.what: Worked out the niche carve cells (north and east, body plus head row) by hand, then wrote the pier body skipping them.
waste.cost: about 10 coordinate-range checks and one retry after the first pass of the head-row rule
waste.tool: A niche-carve helper that returns the air cell list without placing sill or lantern (niche() places them, so it could not be used without stepping on P5). Something like niche.cells(face, box).

waste.what: Hand-wrote the cornice course (stairs on the two street edges, infill between, return column at x95 with its facing) because the cornice() helper takes one box and can't do a return or an open tiling end.
waste.cost: one helper written inline, about 15 lines, plus a facing check for each edge
waste.tool: cornice() with a return option (end column facing into the pier) and an open-end option for bay tiling.

waste.what: Deck slab placement: a loop over x and z with exclusions for the box, figures and the parapet, checked cell by cell against plan.md.
waste.cost: one pass, two exclusion rules; no retries
waste.tool: A deck-cap helper that takes the excluded footprints (planter box, figure cells) as data and returns the slab cells.

waste.what: Verified the tile visually from zoom renders at two positions.
waste.cost: two zoom renders, read by eye
waste.tool: A render or zoom check against a plot's x-range that reports per-bay tiling continuity automatically.

companions.task: Quoin and rustication at the closing pier's NE and SE corners: real long and short course pattern on both faces, not the single-column approximation.
The walkway soffit lanterns (x71..72 z8, x64 z9, plot 2 at x80, y20) and the niche lanterns on the sills, with the no-spawn check on the walkway.
The cornice stairs and return at x95: confirm each upside-down stair's facing toward its back, and the corner joins at z2 and z15.

summary:
Planters, figures, niches: parts/planters.mjs builds the two planter boxes (plots 1 and 2, y 25..32) with eight weeping figures, the plot 2 pier parapet and its two niches (carved by not placing, lantern on sill), and three walkway lanterns at y 20.
make.sh runs clean: 1929 blocks placed by this part, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. check and render show the boxes and figures reading correctly.
Floating-block reports at the figures, niche sills and lanterns are expected: they sit on the cornice (y 24), the end-pier body and the soffit (y 21), which part 4 has not placed yet.
polish: Peristyle part (P4) must leave the end-pier niche cells uncarved: north x 91..93 y 3..12 z 2..3, east x 93..94 y 3..12 z 7..9. Those cells are carved by not placing, so if P4 fills the pier body there, the niche sills and lanterns are blocked.
The three walkway lanterns at (71,20,8), (64,20,9) and (80,20,9) hang from the soffit at y 21, which P4 must place; until then check reports them unsupported.
The niche sills and lanterns (y 3..4) and the figures and planter boxes (y 24 deck) float only until P4 places the pier body and cornice; not a part 5 fault.
Figures on plot 2 (x 80 z 3 and z 14) lean on the box's west wall line rather than a corner, because the spec puts them on x 80; accepted as written.
Box and figure ordering matters: figures must be written before planterBox, since the arm cell sits on the box corner and planterBox writes only into air. Recorded in plan.md Notes.

waste.what: Figure arm directions worked out by hand: each of the eight weeping figures needed its diagonal toward the nearest box corner, plus the figure and box ordering problem found by trial.
waste.cost: about 8 coordinate pairs and two failed builds of reasoning; ordering found only by reading the helper's writer
waste.tool: weepingFigure could take the box rectangle and derive armDir itself (toward the nearest corner of a planterBox), and planterBox could return its corner cells so callers know the order.

waste.what: Niche box coordinates and lantern positions worked out by hand from the plan's z/x ranges, then checked against the helper's carve rule (the top row keeps only the centre cell).
waste.cost: about 6 coordinates computed, 1 check of the helper source
waste.tool: niche() could take the pier's outer face and depth instead of a full box, and return the carved list so the peristyle part can read it from a file (for example niches.json) instead of hard-coding the cells.

waste.what: Walkway hanging lanterns placed with a loop over a hand-written coordinate list, and the soffit dependency checked by reading the fit report, not by a tool.
waste.cost: 3 set() calls and one fit cycle
waste.tool: a lantern helper that checks for a block above and reports the unsupported ones before the merge, with a parts dependency list.

waste.what: make.sh failed once because the vocab barrel does not export B (a bad import), so the first run wasted a cycle; the mcd path was also not word-split in zsh, which cost a second retry.
waste.cost: 2 failed runs
waste.tool: vocab.mjs should re-export the build library's B (or the kit should say B comes from the library), and the kit docs should give mcd as a shell function or a node command, not a $MCD variable.

companions.task: Build the closing pier's body and carve its two niches so the cells are left open without a patch. The niche sills and the lantern standing on each sill need the pier to be solid to y 23.

Shape the four weeping figures per box so the drapery reads as a figure leaning on the box corner, not as stacked pillars. A carver would give each figure a head and a lean, which the white_terracotta column and calcite cap do not show.
Check the soffit lighting at y 20 in the walkway, so each hanging lantern has a block above it and the light map shows no dark cell under the colonnade.

summary:
Exhibition hall and lamps: Exhibition hall bay (plot 3) built in parts/hall.mjs: front wall z4..6 with pilasters, blind arch, frieze, cornice, parapet with sunk panel, back wall, and shed roof via shedRoof; make.sh gives a whole build.nbt with 1631 blocks, no refused writes, no off-palette blocks.
Hall interior lit (floor 8+ except the wall edge) via hanging roof lanterns on sandstone_wall posts; arch-head and pilaster lanterns added; four corner lamp standards at plot 0 corners. mcd fit is OK, and the walk test passes end to end.
Plan Notes updated; elements 16, 17, 19 done and 18 done for the hall (the dome's glowstone belongs to part 3).
polish: Two orphan granite_stairs at (96,24,7) and (111,24,7) from the shed roof's cut-square ends: mcd check reports them as touching the build on one face (the neighbouring bay's cells are not built yet, so this may clear when the peristyle parts land).
Arch-head lantern is at y16 hanging from the keystone wall at y17, not the plan's y15, because y15 had no block above it.
Hall interior lanterns: the posts plus standing lanterns at y1..2 were added beyond the plan's hanging-only spec, to keep the floor lit (hanging alone left it at light 0).
Render check: the hall reads correctly from the north (zoom at 103,12,12); the roof and frieze are not yet checked against the neighbouring bays, which are still stubs in this copy.
Light was measured only on the y1 floor slice; the hall's wall edges at z4..6 still read low (0-3) and are not a walkable path.

waste.what: Tracking which cells the blind arch, roof and wall had taken so the wall fill would skip them, by checking air per cell in a loop.
waste.cost: About 54 skipped writes found only after one run; one debug pass to print them.
waste.tool: A helper that fills a box and skips any cell already occupied, reporting the count and cells; or runParts reporting skipped writes per part.

waste.what: Trial and error on lantern height: hanging lanterns under a 16-high roof left the hall floor at light 0, found only in the light map after the first build.
waste.cost: One full rebuild plus a light map read, then posts added in a second build.
waste.tool: mcd light with a planned-lantern list before the build, or a lantern-spot helper that picks the lowest hang height that keeps the floor at 8+.

waste.what: Finding each roof-end and bracket cell by hand (y and facing) to avoid orphans.
waste.cost: Coordinates worked out by hand for the four pilaster bracket and lantern cells, and the roof-end orphans left unresolved.
waste.tool: shedRoof option for square-cut ends (no orphan at the plot edge), and a bracket helper that places a bracket and its hanging lantern together.

companions.task: Cut the shed roof's ends square at the plot edge so no granite stair sticks out at x 96 and x 111, and set the stair/slab stagger to the plan's 1:2 pitch rather than the helper's default.
Check the blind arch's archivolt and keystone and the frieze tablets for stone courses; the vocab helper gave the shapes, but a mason would confirm the rhythm reads as cut stone.
Confirm the hall shed roof's pitch and where its high edge tucks behind the parapet, as the roof is the one piece built by hand against the helper's default.

summary: room: Rotunda interior: Rotunda interior lit, no furniture (the monument has none): 4 cut_sandstone brackets with hanging lanterns at y 8 on the diagonal pier faces, and 6 standing lanterns on the paving at the octagon corners. Dark floor cells fell from 390 to 21, and make.sh saved a whole build.nbt with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines.
polish: Plan's arch-crown lanterns (hanging at y 24 under each arch, t=0) are not built: at y 25 the arch opening is air, so nothing holds the lantern. It needs the keystone at y 26 from the columns part, then a lantern at y 25.

21 floor cells still read dark (light 0). They are the box corners outside the inner octagon, where the ring is absent in the built ring part, so they are not the interior. The ring part's diagonal test (|dx|+|dz| 31..38 should be ring) leaves air at e.g. (20,1,12); the fix belongs to the ring part, not this room.

`mcd room --only "Rotunda interior"` still says NEEDS WORK: 244 floor cells are unreached, all at y 10 or on the y 34 ledge at the box corners (outside the octagon, ring/attic geometry). The interior octagon itself is reachable through all eight arches.

In this copy the columns, dome and coffers are stubs, so the coffer glowstone and the upper-dome light are unverified; the render shows the ring only. The dome glowstone cannot light the floor anyway (about 50 blocks up), so the floor light comes from the 10 lanterns and the medallion's glowstones.
plan.md has no checklist to tick. elements.md item 18 (lighting) is shared with P6 and P3, so I left it unticked.

waste.what: Chose the floor lantern cells by hand from the room tool's lantern suggestions, then re-ran make and the room check once per change to watch the dark count fall from 390 to 21.
waste.cost: about 4 make+check cycles
waste.tool: `mcd room --apply-lamps` or a `--lamps-json` output that writes the suggested lantern spots as a list the part can import, so the part does not copy coordinates by hand

waste.what: Searched by hand for bracket spots on the diagonal pier faces (wall-adjacent, air above and below, nearest to a mid-face target), since the octagon's inner boundary is not a box; the first search returned only axis-side spots and needed a rewrite.
waste.cost: one generator with a nested loop over the room box, plus one rewrite
waste.tool: a build-library helper like `octFaceSpots(g, centre, rIn, face)` returning wall-adjacent air cells on each octagon face, with clearance from pilasters and arches

waste.what: Worked out by hand which octagon cells are interior (|dx|+|dz|<=30) versus ring versus exterior, to explain the dark box corners.
waste.cost: several blockAt probes on the built file
waste.tool: `mcd room` could print the reason for each dark cell (outside inner octagon / ring gap / exterior) so the corner gap shows at once

companions.task: to place the arch-crown lanterns once the keystone exists, and to confirm the floor lamp spots against the ring's corner geometry before the ring is fixed
to check the octagon corners of the ring part (air where the diagonal ring should close) and set the course that closes them, so no corner cell is left as an exterior gap inside the box

summary:
room: Peristyle walkway: room: Peristyle walkway built in parts/room-2.mjs (no furniture, per the brief): standing lanterns on the paving along z 7 at x 68, 77, 86, 93 light the floor; hanging lanterns at (71,20,8), (64,20,9), (80,20,9) under the soffit.
make.sh saved a whole build.nbt with 7 blocks from this part, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines. The room check reads light min 8, 0 dark.
The walkway's own check is not clean yet: the three hanging lanterns float until the peristyle part builds the soffit at y 21, which I left to that part.
polish: The three hanging lanterns at y 20 (x 71,z 8; x 64,z 9; x 80,z 9) hang from the soffit at y 21, which is the peristyle part's block (plan.md Peristyle facade, soffit row). Until peristyle.mjs builds it, `mcd check` reports them floating and the walk check reports 3 y 21 cells unreached. Peristyle must build the soffit at y 21 over x 64..95, z 7..10.

No `mcd render` of the full build was made for this part, only `mcd rooms` (room.png). The walkway is sparse in the render because the other parts are still stubs, so the look could not be judged yet.

Light comes from the four standing lanterns on the paving, not the hanging ones: a hanging lantern at y 20 cannot reach the floor at y 1. The plan's hanging-lantern-only lighting for the walkway would leave the floor dark, so plan.md should say so.

waste.what: Worked out the standing-lantern spacing by hand: each lantern at floor level lights a diamond of radius 7 (level = 15 - Manhattan distance), so the far row z 10 needs a lantern every 9 cells. I did this arithmetic on paper and then tested it.
waste.cost: about 5 minutes of coordinate and light arithmetic, one make.sh run, one room check
waste.tool: `mcd room` lantern spots printed as a list of coordinates, or a `mcd light --suggest` mode that picks the fewest standing lantern cells to reach a target level on a named floor row

waste.what: Used a plain set() loop for the three hanging lanterns, and a hand-drawn layers() row for the floor lanterns. The row string was built by index arithmetic (x - 64).
waste.cost: 3 set() calls and one 32-char row built in code
waste.tool: layers() accepting x coordinates per row (a sparse spec like {row: z, x: [..]}) so no index arithmetic is needed

waste.what: Read plan.md's Notes section and appended a line by hand, with no template for part notes.
waste.cost: one Read and one Edit
waste.tool: a `mcd note <plan.md> --part N --text ...` helper that appends a tagged note line

companions.task: Given the walkway's floor grid and the lantern budget, pick the standing lantern cells and check each spot's reach to the far row (z 10). I did this arithmetic by hand.
Build the soffit at y 21 over the walkway (x 64..95, z 7..10) so the three hanging lanterns have something to hang from. This is the peristyle part's block, not mine.

summary: lamplighter: room: Rotunda interior: Rotunda interior lit: 8 hanging crown lanterns (one under each inner keystone, y 25) and 10 standing floor lanterns inside the inner octagon. The four floor lamps that sat in diagonal arch mouths are removed. No air floor cell is at light 0; inside the octagon the minimum is 4 and 73% of cells are at 8+. make.sh builds the whole build.nbt, and walkability is unchanged (1714 of 2022 floor cells reachable, as before).
polish: The room tool still prints NEEDS WORK. Its dark count (28) is solid cut_sandstone pilaster feet read as zeros, not air floor; no air floor cell is at 0.

Aim not fully met: 27% of cells inside the inner octagon are dim (4-7), mostly toward the octagon's outer corners. The tool's next suggestions (12,1,20) and (51,1,20) are diagonal arch mouths, which must stay air, so more lamps need the designer to pick corner spots.

Pier brackets at y 9 are not placed. The plan's diagonal face midpoints are arch mouths (|t| = 0), and the flat piers are only |t| 7-8 wide between the arch and the pilasters, so the bracket search finds no spot. The bracket code was removed; the designer decides whether to drop the brackets or move them to the flat piers.

Crown lanterns hang at y 25 under the keystone (y 26), not at y 24 as the plan says: at t = 0 the cell at y 25 is the arch's own air, so there is nothing above a y 24 lantern. Inner faces only. The outer crown lanterns sit outside the room and were not touched.

waste.what: Mirrored the floor lamp pairs by hand (x and z around 31.5) and checked each candidate against the octagon test.

summary: inspection: Fit: the 32 'on a bottom slab' issues were the eight attic statue piers standing on the y34 ledge slabs (columns.mjs placed them before dome.mjs). Fixed by keeping the ledge out of the pier footprints so the pier's own y34 cell is placed. make.sh rebuilds build.nbt; fit reports OK.

Those unreached cells are not a failing room, so per the brief I did not change them. If they matter for the design, they are at x=11 in the rotunda (inner west face near the arch and pilaster cells) and at x 93..95, z 7..10, y 3..5 in the walkway (the end-pier niche area).
Fit header in the earlier run said '32 issues'; the current build reports OK.
